what: JLL is a global commercial property services firm. It manages buildings for owners and occupiers, brokers leases and sales, manages construction projects, and invests in property through LaSalle.
customers: Corporate occupiers, property owners, investors and developers in more than 80 countries.
money: facilities and workplace management for corporate occupiers
property sales, debt placement and advisory
moat: Global outsourcing contracts covering thousands of buildings for multinational occupiers, which take years to tender and longer to move.
risks: Leasing and capital markets revenue fall sharply when interest rates rise and transactions stop
Net margin of about 3% reflects a large pass-through services business
Office property demand remains structurally uncertain
opportunities: Revenue grew about 11% last year and about 8% a year over three years
Analysts see about 19% upside from current levels
Facilities and project management are contracted and far steadier than brokerage
watch: Leasing revenue growth and the resilience margin in Work Dynamics.
